newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese police break up opposition gathering.
newsitem.headline: Burmese police break up opposition gathering.

text.p: Baton-wielding Burmese security police on Saturday broke up a small gathering of supporters of Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party, witnesses and officials said.
About 50 NLD supporters had gathered at a junction in Rangoon about two km (1.2 miles) from Suu Kyi's house on Saturday afternoon to hear deputy NLD chairmen Tin Oo and Kyi Maung speak.
Witnesses said the crowd dispersed peacefully after being requested to leave by the police and Tin Oo.
Crowds gather at the junction every weekend to see if a top NLD leader or Suu Kyi will come and speak.

Suu Kyi, Tin Oo and Kyi Maung used to give regular weekend speeches to supporters at the front gates of Suu Kyi's house, but the military government stopped them in September by blocking access to the road leading to her house.
A statement issued by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), received by Reuters in Bangkok, said the gathering was a sign the NLD was trying to disrupt the peace.

"This move by the NLD showed clear indications that, given the chance, they intended to disrupt the opening ceremonies of the National Sports Festival, so security personnel are now on the alert and carrying out their duties with vigilance to prevent any untoward incidents," the statement said.
The National Sports Festival began on Saturday with a large ceremony that included a torch relay. The torch was due to pass the junction where the NLD supporters were gathered.

The SLORC has blamed the NLD for being involved in and politicising student demonstrations which took place in early December. Suu Kyi has denied involvement but has said she supports the students in their quest for justice.
Several thousand students took to the streets in a series of protests in early December. They were the largest anti-government demonstrations seen since 1988.
The SLORC seized power in 1988 after quashing the demonstrations in a bloody crackdown that left thousands dead or in jail. Students were at the heart of the 1988 uprisings.
Since December, troops are regularly seen in large trucks patrolling Rangoon streets. Tanks are parked at several parts of the city, including the car park in front of City Hall in downtown Rangoon.
